audit_findings.title: The valuation mixes a pre-acquisition earnings numerator with a post-acquisition balance sheet
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $750.0 million purchase price and $403.7 million of acquired six-month sales indicate scale
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor excludes the additional Mexico earnings, acquisition financing interest, and 25% noncontrolling-interest claim, while the cash and debt context is dated after closing.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 2, 2026, we acquired an additional 25 % ownership interest in McCormick de Mexico from Grupo Herdez, for a purchase price of $ 750 million, which increases our ownership to a 75 % controlling interest.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch. Its net direction cannot be established because incremental earnings increase value, while financing interest and earnings attributable to the remaining 25% owner reduce common-shareholder OE. The acquired business contributed 12.4% of six-month sales, making the mismatch reasonably capable of materially changing normalized OE and the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Build post-closing normalized OE from the 2026 filings, including recurring Mexico operating cash generation, acquisition-related interest, maintenance capital expenditure, elimination of the remeasurement gain and transaction items, and deduction of income attributable to the 25% NCI; then rerun all scenarios on that single perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Receivables factoring may have converted financing proceeds into owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $323.1 million increase in sold receivables, equal to 52.1% of the $620.7 million OE anchor; latest unremitted collections were $36.1 million
audit_findings.mechanism: An unreversed increase in receivables sold would inflate operating cash flow and OE; adding cash collected for the receivables purchaser would also overstate the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The proceeds from the sales of receivables are included in cash from operating activities in the consolidated cash flow statement.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation reversed the factoring increase because its line-by-line construction is absent. The possible $323.1 million distortion is nevertheless material relative to the anchor. Separately, the latest filing demonstrates that $36.1 million of cash was held for the financial institution, while the bridge adds gross cash without a matching deduction.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 OE reconciliation from reported operating cash flow and explicitly reverse the change in sold-receivables funding; reconcile the May 2026 $331.2 million cash balance to the $36.1 million remittance obligation and rerun OE and the bridge for confirmed omissions.

audit_findings.title: A material synthetic-lease residual guarantee is outside the recorded lease liability
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $237.2 million guaranteed amount; actual residual shortfall unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any payable residual-value shortfall would be a claim ahead of common equity and should reduce the equity bridge or future OE when measurable.
audit_findings.evidence: The lease arrangement contains a residual value guarantee of 76.5 % of the lessor’s total construction cost, which approximated $ 310 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantee is filed and equals 76.5% of approximately $310 million, but management concluded that a material payment was not probable and no present shortfall is established. It is therefore a forward-looking exposure to monitor through the November 2027 lease expiry, not a demonstrated current valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain an independent current facility valuation, the contractual shortfall formula, renewal or purchase plans, and updated probability estimates; rerun the bridge if a probable or probability-weighted payment becomes supportable.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor contains tax benefits below the stated forward tax burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.6 million of FY2025 discrete tax benefits, equal to 4.4% of the $620.7 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Unremoved discrete benefits or use of the 21.4% reported rate instead of a sustainable tax rate would inflate recurring after-tax OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Specifically, net discrete tax benefits amounted to $27.6 million in 2025, a decrease of $4.1 million from $31.7 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the discrete benefits and a 24.0% expected adjusted 2026 rate, but the supplied valuation does not show whether its OE calculation already removed or normalized them. Consequently, an error is possible but not demonstrated, and the sustainable tax impact—including Mexico—is not fully established.
audit_findings.action: Trace the OE tax line, remove any retained $27.6 million discrete benefit, apply a supportable normalized tax rate to recurring pretax earnings including Mexico, and rerun the scenarios if the anchor changes.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 compensation expense was temporarily depressed
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; performance compensation was only one component of the filed $20.9 million SG&A decrease
audit_findings.mechanism: An expense-trough anchor would overstate sustainable OE and compound that overstatement through projected growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: SG&A expense decreased by $20.9 million in 2025 as compared to 2024, driven primarily by lower performance-based employee compensation expense, lower distribution expense, and CCI-led cost savings including the impact of SG&A streamlining actions, partially offset by increased brand marketing expense and higher selling and marketing costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that lower performance-based compensation contributed to lower FY2025 SG&A and that such expense was expected to rise in 2026. It does not quantify the compensation component or establish how much represents normal cyclicality versus durable savings, so materiality cannot presently be determined.
audit_findings.action: Obtain performance-compensation expense by year, normalize it over a representative incentive cycle, separate durable CCI savings from deferred costs, and rerun the valuation if normalized OE differs materially.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not equal distributable cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $331.2 million bridge exposure, equal to $1.20 per diluted share and 3.7% of $9,052 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Operating cash, foreign-cash repatriation costs, and third-party collections should be excluded from cash added to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of November 30, 2025, we have $1.7 billion of earnings from our non-U.S. subsidiaries and joint ventures that are considered indefinitely reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable portion is unresolved, but even excluding the entire $331.2 million cash balance would reduce base value only from $32.84 to approximately $31.64 per share and the buy-below price from $22.99 to approximately $22.15. That cannot alter the present conclusion relative to the $52.08 market price, although the bridge should still be refined.
audit_findings.action: Identify cash by jurisdiction and ownership, subtract required operating cash and third-party collections, estimate applicable repatriation taxes, and replace gross cash with verified excess distributable cash in the next rerun.
